native_result.query: How does the prevalence of non-native plants introduced via gardening vary based on habitat type?
native_result.HypoA: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats.

## Resultado del análisis (etapa result)

### Hipótesis grounded (respuesta a la pregunta)

"La prevalencia de plantas no nativas introducidas vía jardinería varía fuerte y significativamente entre tipos de hábitat en la provincia de Barcelona. Sobre los 632 plots y 481 registros no nativos (169 jardín, 289 involuntaria, 23 AgriForest), χ²(18) = 75.20, p = 5.83·10⁻⁹, Cramér's V = 0.28; contraste focal jardín vs resto χ²(9) = 48.83, p = 1.79·10⁻⁷, V = 0.32. La proporción agregada de jardín dentro del total no nativo del hábitat (Σ n.gard/Σ n.total) es máxima en los hábitats húmedos y costeros — Humedales 55.8 % (IC95 % bootstrap = 41.1-73.2 %; Firth OR vs Urbano = 2.94, p = 0.0011) y Costero 53.5 % (37.8-68.8 %; OR = 2.68, p = 0.0052) — intermedia en Ripario 36.5 % (26.7-47.3 %), Urbano 29.8 % y Cultivos 18.5 % (12.8-24.8 %), y exploratoriamente alta en Bosques de coníferas 87.5 % (Σ = 8 registros, Firth OR = 11.7, p = 0.011). Los Cultivos son el único hábitat donde la vía involuntaria (76.9 %) supera dominante a la jardinería. Los contrastes pareados ajustados por Benjamini-Hochberg destacan Wetlands vs Croplands (p_BH = 0.0002), Coastal vs Croplands (p_BH = 0.0006), Wetlands vs Urban (p_BH = 0.011), Coastal vs Urban (p_BH = 0.024), Riparian vs Croplands (p_BH = 0.024) y Coniferous vs Urban (p_BH = 0.043). El GLM binomial-negativo con offset log(n.total) y covariables (elevación, uso urbano/cultivo 2009 a 500 m, distancia a carretera, temperatura) replica el patrón (las covariables apenas añaden información más allá del hábitat; LRT ΔLL = 2.91, gl = 5, p = 0.713). El análisis de sensibilidad restringido a los seis hábitats con Σ n.total ≥ 10 mantiene la asociación (χ²(5) = 31.42, p = 7.74·10⁻⁶, V = 0.26) y el mismo ranking (Wetlands > Cultivos, Coastal > Cultivos, etc.). En síntesis, la presencia de la jardinería como vía de invasión es máxima en hábitats húmedos y costeros, intermedia en urbanos y mínima en cultivos; los bosques densos muestran una señal Jardín muy alta pero con muy pocos registros, por lo que su conclusión debe etiquetarse como exploratoria."

### Tabla resumen final por hábitat

| Hábitat | n_plots | sum_gard / sum_total | %jardín | IC95 % bootstrap | Firth OR vs Urbano | RR NB vs Urbano | Categoría |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|:---:|:---:|---|
| Broad-leaved forests | 68 | 4 / 4 | 100.0 % | 0.00-1.00 | ND | 2.37 | exploratorio |
| Coniferous forests | 77 | 7 / 8 | 87.5 % | 0.60-1.00 | 11.70 (p=.011) | 2.15 | exploratorio |
| Wetlands | 38 | 29 / 52 | 55.8 % | 0.41-0.73 | 2.94 (p=.0011) | 2.03 | principal |
| Coastal | 29 | 23 / 43 | 53.5 % | 0.38-0.69 | 2.68 (p=.0052) | 1.89 | principal |
| Scrublands | 106 | 2 / 5 | 40.0 % | 0.00-1.00 | 1.67 (p=.58) | 0.92 | exploratorio |
| Riparian | 61 | 35 / 96 | 36.5 % | 0.27-0.47 | 1.35 (p=.28) | 1.09 | principal |
| Meadows | 39 | 4 / 13 | 30.8 % | 0.00-0.54 | 1.11 (p=.87) | 0.67 | principal |
| Urban | 65 | 45 / 151 | 29.8 % | 0.22-0.38 | 1.00 (ref) | 1.00 | principal |
| Croplands | 92 | 20 / 108 | 18.5 % | 0.13-0.25 | 0.54 (p=.044) | 0.50 | principal |
| Rock outcrops | 57 | 0 / 1 | 0.0 % | 0.00-0.00 | ND | 0.00 | exploratorio |

### Métricas de evidencia (todas sobre `data/invaded_niche_pathways.csv`)

- **Chi² global (3 vías × 10 hábitats):** χ²(18) = 75.20, p = 5.83·10⁻⁹, V = 0.28, n = 481.
- **Chi² jardín vs resto (2 × 10):** χ²(9) = 48.83, p = 1.79·10⁻⁷, V = 0.32.
- **GLM binomial Firth (8 hábitats, sin separación):** Urban referencia p_jardín = 29.9 %; Humedales β = +1.08 (OR = 2.94, p = 0.0011); Costero β = +0.99 (OR = 2.68, p = 0.0052); Cultivos β = -0.61 (OR = 0.54, p = 0.044); Coniferous β = +2.46 (OR = 11.70, p = 0.011).
- **GLM binomial-negativo (offset + 5 covariables):** RR jardinería vs Urban = 2.03 en humedales (p = 0.069), 1.89 en costero (p = 0.15), 2.15 en coniferous (p = 0.28), 0.50 en cultivos (p = 0.094); convariables no significativas (LRT p = 0.71).
- **Tukey HSD sobre mean(n.gard):** 24 de 45 contrastes significativos al 5 %; el top incluye Wetlands vs Croplands y Coastal vs Croplands.
- **Análisis de sensibilidad (6 hábitats con Σ n.total ≥ 10):** χ² jardín vs resto = 31.42, p = 7.74·10⁻⁶, V = 0.26; Firth mantiene direcciones y Wetlands > Urban (p = 0.011) y Croplands < Urban (p = 0.044).

### Limitaciones / incertidumbres declaradas

- **5 hábitats con Σ n.total < 10** (Rock outcrops=1, Broad-leaved forests=4, Scrublands=5, Coniferous forests=8, Meadows=13): etiquetados como exploratorios; sus proporciones puntuales no son estables.
- **Separación perfecta** en GLM binomial estándar para Broad-leaved forests (100 % jardín, n=4) y Rock outcrops (100 % involuntaria, n=1); se abordó con Firth penalizado sobre los 8 hábitats restantes.
- **Pseudoreplicación espacial:** plots cercanos comparten coordenadas/clima; no se modeló autocorrelación espacial en este análisis.
- **Covariables paisajísticas** (urbanización, cultivos, elevación, distancia a carretera, temperatura) no aportan información significativa sobre el efecto-hábitat (LRT p = 0.71), lo que sugiere que el "hábito" recoge la mayor parte de la varianza explicada más allá del muestreo.
- **El dataset `invasion_success_pathways.csv` (81 spp.)** sólo se usó como contexto: las 42 spp. de jardín son mayoritariamente perennes/arbustos (38/42), con alta reproducción vegetativa (22/42) — útil para perfilar rasgos, no para estimar prevalencia.
- **Tendencia temporal** del dataset `temporal_trends` (jardinería crece de 18 antes 1500 → 397 en 1985-2019, multiplicación × 22) condiciona la prevalencia actual pero no se usó como covariable.

### Artefactos entregables (en `analysis/`)

- Scripts reproducibles: `01_descriptive_and_chi2.py`, `firth_model.py`, `nb_model.py`, `sensitivity.py`, `finalize.py`, `analysis_notebook.py`, orquestados por `run_all.py`. Módulo de soporte: `firth_logistic.py`.
- Tablas en `analysis/tables/`: `final_descriptives.csv`, `final_descriptives_with_ci.csv`, `final_chi2.csv`, `final_pearson_residuals.csv`, `share_within_habitat.csv`, `share_by_pathway.csv`, `final_firth_coefs.csv`, `final_firth_predictions.csv`, `final_firth_pairwise.csv`, `final_firth_sens_coefs.csv`, `final_firth_sens_predictions.csv`, `final_nb_coefs.csv`, `final_tukey_meangard.csv`, `final_tukey_sens.csv`, `final_sensitivity_chi2.csv`, `final_sensitivity_bootstrap.csv`, `summary_by_habitat.csv`, `hypothesis.txt`, `supporting_stats.json`, `sensitivity_filter.json`.
- Logs de ejecución: `analysis/logs_pipeline.txt`, `analysis/logs_01.txt`, etc.

### Workflow ejecutado (resumen)

1. Inspección de `invaded_niche_pathways.csv` (632 plots, 37 columnas, separador TSV con quoting). Verificación `n.total = n.gard + n.unint + n.agfo` en 100 % de filas.
2. Descriptivos por hábitat + bootstrap IC95 % (B=2000) sobre Σ n.gard, mean(n.gard), y proporción Σ n.gard/Σ n.total.
3. Chi-cuadrado de independencia (3 × 10 y 2 × 10) con cálculo de residuos de Pearson.
4. GLM binomial penalizado por Firth (implementación propia en `firth_logistic.py`) sobre 8 hábitats, evitando separación perfecta.
5. Contrastes por pares del GLM Firth con ajuste Benjamini-Hochberg (28 contrastes, 7 significativos al 5 %).
6. GLM binomial-negativo con offset log(n.total) y 5 covariables paisajísticas estandarizadas; LRT para covariables.
7. Tukey HSD sobre mean(n.gard) entre los 10 hábitats.
8. Análisis de sensibilidad restringido a 6 hábitats con Σ n.total ≥ 10 (excluidos los 5 más pequeños).
9. Consolidación final en `summary_by_habitat.csv` y `hypothesis.txt`.

sub_hypo.text: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats.
sub_hypo.context: Non-native plants introduced through gardening in the Barcelona province.
sub_hypo.relations: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats; the direction of the difference is unspecified.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats.

sub_hypo.text: Introduction-pathway composition, particularly the proportion of gardening introductions, differs significantly among habitat types.
sub_hypo.context: Non-native plants in 632 plots across ten habitat types in Barcelona province, comprising 481 records: 169 gardening, 289 unintentional, and 23 agriculture/forestry introductions.
sub_hypo.relations: Habitat and introduction pathway are associated: global χ²(18) = 75.20, p = 5.83×10⁻⁹, Cramér's V = 0.28; gardening versus other pathways χ²(9) = 48.83, p = 1.79×10⁻⁷, V = 0.32. Gardening prevalence is defined as Σ n.gard / Σ n.total within each habitat.

sub_hypo.text: Among habitats with at least ten non-native records, gardening prevalence is highest in wetlands and coastal habitats, intermediate in riparian, meadow, and urban habitats, and lowest in croplands.
sub_hypo.context: Barcelona province; wetlands, coastal habitats, riparian habitats, meadows, urban habitats, and croplands, each with Σ n.total ≥ 10.
sub_hypo.relations: Gardening proportions are wetlands 55.8%, coastal 53.5%, riparian 36.5%, meadows 30.8%, urban 29.8%, and croplands 18.5%. Firth odds ratios relative to urban habitats are 2.94 for wetlands (p = 0.0011), 2.68 for coastal habitats (p = 0.0052), and 0.54 for croplands (p = 0.044). BH-adjusted contrasts support wetlands > croplands (p = 0.0002), coastal > croplands (p = 0.0006), wetlands > urban (p = 0.011), coastal > urban (p = 0.024), and riparian > croplands (p = 0.024). Restriction to these six habitats retains the association: χ²(5) = 31.42, p = 7.74×10⁻⁶, V = 0.26.

sub_hypo.text: Forest habitats show very high gardening proportions, but these findings are exploratory because they rely on very few non-native records.
sub_hypo.context: Broad-leaved and coniferous forests in the sampled Barcelona-province plots.
sub_hypo.relations: Gardening accounts for 4/4 records in broad-leaved forests and 7/8 records in coniferous forests. Coniferous forests have a Firth odds ratio of 11.70 relative to urban habitats (p = 0.011; BH-adjusted pairwise p = 0.043). Broad-leaved forests exhibit perfect separation and were excluded, together with rock outcrops, from the eight-habitat Firth analysis; sparse records limit interpretation.

sub_hypo.text: Unintentional introductions dominate gardening introductions in croplands.
sub_hypo.context: Cropland plots in Barcelona province, with 108 non-native records.
sub_hypo.relations: Unintentional introductions constitute 76.9% of cropland non-native records, compared with 18.5% introduced through gardening.

sub_hypo.text: The habitat-specific gardening pattern persists after adjustment for landscape and environmental covariates, which add little explanatory information beyond habitat.
sub_hypo.context: Barcelona-province plots analyzed using a negative-binomial GLM with log(n.total) as an offset and five standardized covariates; spatial autocorrelation was not modeled.
sub_hypo.relations: Adjusted gardening rate ratios relative to urban habitats are 2.03 for wetlands (p = 0.069), 1.89 for coastal habitats (p = 0.15), 2.15 for coniferous forests (p = 0.28), and 0.50 for croplands (p = 0.094), reproducing the directional pattern without individually significant contrasts at 5%. Adding the five covariates provides no significant improvement (reported LRT ΔLL = 2.91, df = 5, p = 0.713).
